h: Shabbos Holiness Guards Yisrael Against the Spread of Impurity

p: In this parsha there is mentioned once again
why did it repeat the mitzvah a second time
"'And the land become full of lewdness' (19:29),
to say: the plague of the year is the festival,
when they eat and drink, etc.,
'Harlotry, wine and new wine take away the heart.'"
But in truth in the Gemara
that is, the festivals and not Shabbos;
for the eating of Shabbos does no harm
in causing the evil inclination to rule,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח, ב)
"'The dung of your festivals' (Malachi 2:3), it says,
and not 'the dung of your Shabbosos';
whereas Shabbos it does not say."
That is, the holiness of the festivals
this is not so with the holiness of Shabbos,
"For I am Hashem Who sanctifies you";
that one eats on Shabbos for bodily pleasure
that the delights of Shabbos would cause
the land to become full of lewdness.
And in truth even regarding the festivals
לֹא אָמְרוּ הָא דְּסִקְבָּא דְּשַׁתָּא רִגְלָא
they did not say "the plague of the year is the festival"
for it is for this reason
that they instituted fasting on Monday-Thursday-Monday
וְלֹא תִּקְּנוּ אֶלָּא אַחַר פֶּסַח וְסוּכּוֹת
and they instituted it only after Pesach and Sukkos
וְעַיֵּין בֵּית יוֹסֵף אוֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן תכט)
and see Beis Yosef, Orach Chaim 429).
It is clear that they instituted it only there
they did not practice fasting after it;
and all the more so Shabbos,
since we find in the language of the verse
גַּם עַל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה (נְחֶמְיָה ח, י)
for the day is holy to our Lord"
all the more so on the other festivals:
and the drinking of a mitzvah will not bring
that on Shabbos, when Yisrael eat and drink,
they begin with words of Torah, etc.;
for even though they then partook
of the feast of that wicked one,
nevertheless by the power of the holiness of Shabbos
they opened their mouths with words of Torah
which does not have as much holiness
and from the Torah it is permitted on Chol HaMoed
and it is forbidden only rabbinically.
And in truth it says in the Yerushalmi
because people eat and drink and act frivolously.
But the eating and rejoicing of Yom Tov
and therefore they did not institute the fast
is meant also for the festivals,
for besides that in any case
and also according to what I wrote,
גַּם עַל יוֹם טוֹב עַצְמוֹ לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ
it does not apply even to Yom Tov itself;
is the term only for Yom Tov,
here it is written in the term "My Shabbosos,"
and the festivals are not called "My Shabbosos,"
for they derive from the holiness of Yisrael,
and on account of the miracles
done for Yisrael at that time
by the command of Hashem Yisbarach;
and only Shabbos is called "a Shabbos to Hashem"
at the beginning of Parshas Vayakhel,
at the beginning of the passage of the offerings,
and at the end of the passage of the offerings:
and in Parshas Ki Sisa it is called "My Shabbosos";
and because on it Hashem Yisbarach rested
And about this it says in Toras Kohanim,
of which it says "a Shabbos to Hashem,"
and as the Ramban writes there;
that through two Shabbosos they are redeemed,
and so in the Introduction to the Zohar (5b)
it explains "My Shabbosos," in the plural,
that it means also the festivals,
and this is as I wrote,
they are not called "My Shabbosos" at all.
that the matter is the reverse:
for the language of the verse there before it,
by making her a harlot, etc.,
and the land become full of lewdness,"
she will cause the whole land to be filled
in all the souls of Yisrael,
for all Yisrael are like one body,
and as is known the parable of the Midrash
of one who bores a hole in a ship.
to cleanse oneself of the evil thoughts,
וְהַיְינוּ כִּדְאִיתָא בְּרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שָׁם
That is, as the Ramban, of blessed memory, says there,
that by way of the truth it commands
and regarding the Shabbos that is His Sanctuary.
And his intent is to what the holy Zohar writes
this is the Shabbos of Erev Shabbos,
That is, from the side of the holiness
there is the fear and awe
immediately at the onset of Shabbos,
"We shall serve with fear and awe";
and the holiness of the awe
before Him, may He be blessed,
יֵצֶר טוֹב עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע כוּ׳
his good inclination against the evil inclination, etc.";
to cast upon it trembling and fear.)
a person will cleanse and purify his heart
and "the tzaddik will hold to his way"
"To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you";
and they will be saved from being corrupted, Heaven forbid.
that is, that they will merit fear,
and it is written, "I am Hashem."
And at the head of the parsha it is written:
for I, Hashem your God, am holy."
And ten times there is mentioned in this parsha
as is written in the Baal HaTurim;
וְכֵן כְּתִיב גַּם כֵּן בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ
and likewise it is written in this parsha
"Every man shall fear his mother and his father,
and you shall keep My Shabbosos";
from his own side in the fear of Hashem;
the fear of father and mother
they will merit the holiness from Hashem Yisbarach,
which is the holiness of Shabbos,
as it is written, "For I am Hashem Who sanctifies you."
for although fear is from the side of man,
"Everything is in the hands of Heaven
that it too is from Hashem Yisbarach;
and this is "I am Hashem your God,"
Who is the Master of all powers;
for even the fear that is from the side of man
הוּא גַּם כֵּן מֵעֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
is also from the help of Hashem Yisbarach.
of the holiness of Hashem Yisbarach from His side,
for it is known and plain
that it is only from Hashem Yisbarach.
And the last time that there is mentioned,
"Who has separated you from the peoples"
you should know that this too
is from the help of Hashem Yisbarach:
"And you shall be holy to Me,
and I have separated you from the peoples"
(שְׁמוּאֵל א ב, ט) רַגְלֵי חֲסִידָיו יִשְׁמוֹר
"guards the feet of His pious ones" (Shmuel I 2:9),
(תְּהִלִּים לז, לג) וַה׳ לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְּיָדוֹ
and "Hashem will not abandon him into his hand" (Tehillim 37:33);
for Hashem Yisbarach from His side
so that they will not, Heaven forbid, be assimilated
rather, "and I have separated you from the peoples."
For even in the land of Egypt,
where they were like a fetus in its mother's womb,
"a nation from the midst of a nation,"
"Thus says Hashem, the God of Yisrael:
For although the Holy One, blessed be He,
does not attach His Name to the tzaddikim in their lifetime,
"Behold, He does not trust His holy ones"
(as is written in Rashi's commentary in Vayeitzei
so how could Hashem Yisbarach attach
that, Heaven forbid, there will not be corrupted
וְאָנֹכִי ה׳ אֱלֹקֶיךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם וְגוֹ׳
"'And I am Hashem your God from the land of Egypt, etc.' (Hoshea 13:4):
it does not say 'Who took you out,' etc.
Was it only from the land of Egypt
that they had a King, etc.?
that Yisrael existed in the world,
the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He,
except in the land of Egypt,
where they were in hard labor, etc.,
and they did not change from their own custom
That is, Yisrael were distinguished there
and were not, Heaven forbid, assimilated
"Do not fear to go down to Egypt,
for I will make you a great nation there."
For in Egypt they became a nation,
and Klal Yisrael came into being;
where they were like a fetus in its mother's womb;
וְזֶה מִצַּד כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי ה׳
and this is from the side of "For I, Hashem, am holy."
And it is implied in the Midrash
which writes: "A parable — to what is the matter comparable?
To a king who betrothed a woman:
since you have been betrothed to My Name, etc.,
just as I am holy, etc."
which implies that even without effort on their part
And this is what it says:
"And you shall be holy to Me,
all from the side of Hashem Yisbarach
that they will be separated from the peoples
for His Name, may He be blessed.

paragraphs.text: Source: Iyov 15:15 — “הן בקדשו לא יאמין ושמים לא זכו בעיניו” — “[God] puts no trust in the holy ones; The heavens are not guiltless in God’s sight;”

paragraphs.text: Source: Bereishis Rabbah 94:9 — “… ומתתיהו, חמשה בפרט, ובכללן ששה. אלא אף (דברי הימים א כה, יז): שמעי, מנאו הקדוש ברוך הוא עד שהוא במעי אמו. ואם יאמר לך אדם עשירי שמעי, אמר לו עשירי …” — ““All the people who were coming with Jacob to Egypt, the products of his loins, aside from the wives of Jacob's sons; all the people were sixty-six” (Genesis 46:26). “And the sons of Joseph, who were born to him in …”

paragraphs.text: Source: Bereishis 46:3 — “ויאמר אנכי האל אלהי אביך אל תירא מרדה מצרימה כי לגוי גדול אשימך שם” — ““I am God, the God of your father’s [house]. Fear not to go down to Egypt, for I will make you there into a great nation.”
